Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Key needs: lower-latency real-time inference for payments routing, strong audit logs for compliance, and a predictable pricing model for a growing trial.
- Success criteria for proof-of-concept (POC): sub-120ms p95 on our standard routing workload, SOC 2 evidence for security checklist items, and a clear path to scale to 50M tokens/mo.
- Mutual action plan (attached): schedule technical deep-dive with your engineering team, agree on trial scope, and get legal/ procurement NDAs in place.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive — week of Mar 7 (30–45m) — suggested attendees: Lukas (solutions), Rishi (solutions architect), your infra lead
2) POC scope doc by Mar 4 — I’ll share a draft attached
3) Contract/ procurement — Priya, looping you for legal/contact at FinTechCo

Could you confirm timing and whether the above still reflects priority for Q2? If it’s better to revisit later, just say so — we’ll adjust cadence.

Attachments: 2027-03-01-FinTechCo-MAP.pdf (draft mutual action plan)

Thanks,

Quick thoughts from infra/solutions:
- The sub-120ms p95 target is achievable on our Dedicated or optimized Hosted configuration given their QPS profile, but we’ll need to instrument realistic traffic and KV cache priming during the POC.
- For the initial deep-dive, I recommend we include an ops/infra contact — I can take the lead on a short checklist: instance sizing, quantization profile (8-bit), and traffic shaping to simulate spikes.
- Potential risk: if their input sequence lengths spike >1k tokens we should surface fallback plans in the MAP.

I’ll draft a 1-page technical note and attach here for Marissa to include in the POC scope. Attaching: FinTechCo-technical-notes-20270302.pdf
